en.display_text:
How many of the following statements about the connection between the Extremist Constructive Swadeshi program and Gandhian nationalism are correct?

1. Tilak's emphasis on self-sufficiency through indigenous industries under 'Constructive Swadeshi' is recognized as an anticipation of Gandhi's khadi and cottage industry program.
2. Bipin Chandra Pal's advocacy of 'complete non-cooperation' with colonial institutions anticipated the method, if not the precise philosophical grounding, of Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement.
3. Lala Lajpat Rai's social reform work through Arya Samaj was directly adopted by Gandhi as the philosophical basis for the Constructive Programme of the 1930s.
4. The Extremist phase's emphasis on mass political participation, as distinct from elite petitioning, is recognized as a methodological precursor to Gandhi's mass civil disobedience campaigns.

(a) Only one
(b) Only two
(c) Only three
(d) All four

statement_analysis.statement: Tilak's emphasis on self-sufficiency through indigenous industries under 'Constructive Swadeshi' is recognized as an anticipation of Gandhi's khadi and cottage industry program.
statement_analysis.reason: Historians explicitly identify the continuity between Extremist constructive Swadeshi (indigenous industries, national banks) and Gandhi's khadi-centered constructive program.

statement_analysis.statement: Bipin Chandra Pal's advocacy of 'complete non-cooperation' with colonial institutions anticipated the method, if not the precise philosophical grounding, of Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement.
statement_analysis.reason: Pal's non-cooperation concept is documented as a precursor to Gandhian non-cooperation — the method (withdrawal of cooperation from colonial institutions) is similar even if the philosophical roots differ.

statement_analysis.statement: Lala Lajpat Rai's social reform work through Arya Samaj was directly adopted by Gandhi as the philosophical basis for the Constructive Programme of the 1930s.
statement_analysis.reason: Gandhi's constructive program drew on his own Ruskin/Tolstoy-influenced philosophy and Vedantic thought — not specifically on Arya Samaj; claiming direct adoption misrepresents the relationship.

statement_analysis.statement: The Extremist phase's emphasis on mass political participation, as distinct from elite petitioning, is recognized as a methodological precursor to Gandhi's mass civil disobedience campaigns.
statement_analysis.reason: This continuity is consistently acknowledged by historians — the Extremists shifted Indian politics from elite lobbying to mass agitation, creating the template Gandhi subsequently scaled up.

en.strong_distractor: c — Students uncertain about Statement 3 (Arya Samaj's direct role in Gandhi's program) may tentatively accept it, yielding 'Only three' as a plausible answer.
elimination_logic: Confirm Statement 1: Continuity between constructive Swadeshi and Gandhi's khadi program is historically established — correct.
Confirm Statement 2: Pal's non-cooperation as precursor is documented — correct.
Examine Statement 3: Gandhi did not adopt Arya Samaj as the basis of his constructive program — this overstates the connection; incorrect.
Confirm Statement 4: Extremist shift to mass politics as Gandhi precursor is documented — correct.
Three statements correct (1, 2, 4) — 'Only three' — option (c).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 3 uses the scope-extension technique: Arya Samaj did influence social reform in the nationalist period, and Lajpat Rai was a prominent reformer — but claiming Gandhi 'directly adopted' Arya Samaj philosophy for his Constructive Programme is an overstatement. Gandhi's philosophical sources were diverse and specifically did not include Arya Samaj's Vedic orthodoxy.
en.final_explanation: The Extremist-Gandhi continuity question requires granular distinctions. Statement 1 is correct — constructive Swadeshi's indigenous industries directly anticipate Gandhi's khadi program. Statement 2 is correct — Pal's complete non-cooperation is a documented methodological precursor. Statement 3 is incorrect — Gandhi's constructive program drew on Ruskin's 'Unto This Last,' Tolstoy's ideas, and his own Vedantic synthesis; Arya Samaj philosophy was not its basis. Statement 4 is correct — the shift from elite petitioning to mass political participation is Extremism's most lasting methodological contribution. Three statements (1, 2, 4) are correct — option (c). • Value Addition: • Gandhi read John Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' on a train journey in 1904 — it profoundly shaped his constructive program. • Extremist mass mobilization relied on religious festivals; Gandhi replaced this with cross-religious symbols and hartal. • The Constructive Programme of the 1940s (Gandhi's pamphlet) explicitly includes khadi, village industries, village sanitation, and Hindu-Muslim unity.

statement_analysis.reason: गांधी का निर्माणात्मक कार्यक्रम उनके स्वयं के रस्किन/टॉलस्टॉय-प्रभावित दर्शन और वेदांत विचारों पर आधारित था — विशेष रूप से आर्य समाज पर नहीं; सीधे अपनाने का दावा संबंध को गलत प्रस्तुत करता है।

elimination_logic: कथन 1 की पुष्टि करें: निर्माणात्मक स्वदेशी और गांधी के खादी कार्यक्रम के बीच निरंतरता ऐतिहासिक रूप से स्थापित है — सही।
कथन 2 की पुष्टि करें: पाल का असहयोग पूर्वधारणा के रूप में प्रलेखित है — सही।
कथन 3 की जांच करें: गांधी ने अपने निर्माणात्मक कार्यक्रम के आधार के रूप में आर्य समाज को अपनाया नहीं — यह संबंध अतिशयोक्ति है; गलत।

तीन कथन सही हैं (1, 2, 4) — 'केवल तीन' — विकल्प (c)।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 3 में स्कोप-एक्सटेंशन तकनीक का उपयोग किया गया है: आर्य समाज ने राष्ट्रीय काल में सामाजिक सुधार को प्रभावित किया था, और लाजपत राय एक प्रमुख सुधारक थे — लेकिन यह दावा कि गांधी ने अपने निर्माणात्मक कार्यक्रम के लिए आर्य समाज के दर्शन को 'सीधे अपनाया' अतिशयोक्ति है। गांधी के दार्शनिक स्रोत विविध थे और विशेष रूप से आर्य समाज की वैदिक रूढ़िवादिता शामिल नहीं थी।

statement_analysis.statement: Tilak's slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it' expressed a rights-based claim to self-governance that rejected the premise that Indians needed to prove their readiness for self-rule.

Statements 1 and 2 correct — option (a).

Students who internalize Extremists as 'total rejectionists' based on their aggressive rhetoric may not recall that Extremists continued to participate in legislative councils while simultaneously advocating mass pressure. The critique was methodological, not categorical.
en.final_explanation: The Extremist ideological critique of Moderatism had two core dimensions. Statement 1 is correct: 'mendicancy' was the Extremist label for Moderate petitioning — they argued thirty years of prayers had produced minimal results. Statement 2 is correct: Tilak's birthright slogan transformed the self-rule debate from 'fitness for governance' (colonial-Moderate framing) to 'inherent right regardless of readiness' — a fundamentally different political logic. Statement 3 is incorrect: Extremists did not reject all institutional engagement; they participated in councils while advocating mass agitation as a pressure mechanism. The 'birthright' assertion was about method and dignity, not about boycotting all colonial institutions. en.strong_distractor: b — Students who know the Partition was reversed 'after significant agitation' and associate the Congress Lucknow session (1916) with nationalists' gains may project the annulment onto 1916.

en.upsc_trap_explanation: The temporal-swap trap offers 1905 (Partition year), 1908 (Extremist peak), and 1916 (Lucknow Pact) as plausible distractors, with 1911 being the correct year. Students who associate the annulment with 'Congress pressure' may project it onto a Congress session year rather than the Coronation Durbar year.
en.final_explanation: The Partition of Bengal was implemented in October 1905 by Lord Curzon, dividing Bengal into two provinces. Option (a) is wrong — 1905 is the Partition year, not the annulment. Option (b) is wrong — 1916 saw the Lucknow Pact and Home Rule Leagues, not the Bengal Partition annulment. Option (c) is wrong — 1908 was marked by Tilak's second sedition trial and the Alipore Bomb Case. Option (d) is correct: the Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911 and announced at the Delhi Coronation Durbar of King George V. • Value Addition: • The 1911 annulment created the new province of Bihar and Orissa and a reconstituted Bengal. • The Delhi Durbar of 1911 also announced the transfer of capital from Calcutta to Delhi. • British official justification for annulment was administrative rationalization, not concession to nationalist pressure — though nationalists claimed credit.

en.final_explanation: The Bal-Pal-Lal trio had distinct ideological signatures despite their common Extremist platform. Lala Lajpat Rai (C) is correctly matched with Arya Samaj roots, Punjab labor movements, and 'Unhappy India' (his 1928 rebuttal to Katherine Mayo) — C-1. The four-fold Extremist program (Boycott, Swadeshi, National Education, Self-Government) was the collective platform — D-3. hi.final_explanation: बाल-पाल-लाल त्रयी के पास उनके सामान्य उग्रवादी मंच के बावजूद विशिष्ट वैचारिक पहचान थी। तिलक (A) को सही ढंग से 'गीता रहस्य' और गणपति/शिवाजी त्योहार रणनीति से जोड़ा गया है — सांस्कृतिक संगठना उनकी मुख्य विधि थी (A-2)। बिपिन चंद्र पाल (B) को वेदांत आध्यात्मिक राष्ट्रवाद और भारत के संघीय दृष्टिकोण से सही ढंग से जोड़ा गया है — उनकी वैचारिक विशिष्टता (B-4)। लाला लाजपत राय (C) को आर्य समाज की जड़ें, पंजाब श्रमिक आंदोलन, और 'अनहैप्पी इंडिया' (1928 में कैथरीन मेयो के दावों का खंडन) से सही जोड़ा गया है — C-1। चार-गुणात्मक उग्रवादी कार्यक्रम (बहिष्कार, स्वदेशी, राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा, स्वशासन) सामूहिक मंच था — D-3। सही मिलान: A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3 — विकल्प (b)। • अतिरिक्त जानकारी: • 'गीता रहस्य' तिलक ने मंडले (1908–1914) में कारावास के दौरान लिखा था। • पाल का संघीय दृष्टिकोण उस समय के लिए असामान्य था — अधिकांश राष्ट्रवादी एकात्मक भारतीय राज्य की कल्पना करते थे। • लाजपत राय की 'अनहैप्पी इंडिया' विशेष रूप से कैथरीन मेयो के यह दावा खंडित करती है कि भारतीय गरीबी और सामाजिक कुप्रथाएँ स्व-निर्मित हैं।
